title: A code path implies acceptance
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume that $N$ decides $L$ in space $sp$. For a Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $s,u,v$, suppose $u$ is the code of the initial configuration on $x$ within window $s$, there is a finite sequence of zero or more valid one-step transitions within that window from the configuration coded by $u$ to the one coded by $v$, and $v$ is the code of a halted configuration with output exactly $[1]$ within that window. Then $x\in L$.
hypotheses_covered: N decides L in space sp
Natural numbers s, u, and v
The initial-configuration encoding for x, u, and s belongs to the initial language
There is a reflexive-transitive sequence of valid coded steps from u to v at window size s
The acceptance encoding for x, v, and s belongs to the acceptance language
